diagrams.title: Broker Capacity Without Losing Control of Consumption
diagrams.subtitle: Five operating stages connect supplier rights to reconciled customer usage.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The operator resells only contractually authorized capacity. Prepayment controls credit exposure but does not eliminate chargebacks, supplier commits, or service-credit obligations.
diagrams.caption: Keep gross customer billings, upstream supplier charges, and retained contribution in separate ledger accounts. A customer's wallet deposit is not earned service revenue before delivery.

stages.label: Secure supply rights
stages.value: Document capacity, resale rights, and supplier limits
stages.detail: Negotiate GPU reservation windows, carrier termination rates, IPv4 lease authority, cancellation terms, and measurable SLAs. Track minimum commits separately from consumed units.

stages.label: Screen and fund
stages.value: Identify buyers before activating prepaid consumption limits
stages.detail: Verify business identity and intended workloads, enforce the AUP, and fund a Stripe-backed internal credit ledger. Reject abusive mining, spoofing, and unauthorized calling.

stages.label: Route and isolate
stages.value: Allocate eligible workloads within explicit spend ceilings
stages.detail: Use LiteLLM or vLLM for supported inference paths and least-cost routing for eligible SIP routes. Apply tenant isolation, destination restrictions, and tested failover limits.

stages.label: Meter and reconcile
stages.value: Match customer usage with independent supplier records
stages.detail: Combine request-level token records, scheduler allocation intervals, DCGM health telemetry, and carrier call-detail records. DCGM utilization alone is not a billing ledger.

stages.label: Collect and rebalance
stages.value: Recognize delivered service and reset exposure daily
stages.detail: Debit wallets idempotently, recognize delivered units, reconcile supplier invoices, and stop consumption at limits. Reprice expiring GPU reservations before generation-driven price compression erases their spread.

diagrams.title: One Cohort, Five Observable Conversion Steps
diagrams.subtitle: Track qualified demand before increasing noncancelable capacity.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Illustrative 90-day acquisition cohort, not a revenue forecast. Every stage is a subset of the preceding stage; all counts represent buyer organizations rather than contacts or API keys.
diagrams.caption: The cohort narrows 200 → 80 → 40 → 20 → 10. Sequential conversion is 40%, 50%, 50%, and 50%; overall conversion is 5%. Ten repeat buyers do not by themselves establish $675,000 billings.

stages.label: Documented prospects
stages.value: 200 organizations with observable recurring capacity needs
stages.detail: Build a named account list from permitted research and existing relationships. Record workload type, buyer role, current supplier arrangement, and likely purchasing window.

stages.label: Qualified demand
stages.value: 80 organizations with budget and technical fit
stages.detail: Forty percent of the original cohort confirms budget, eligible destinations, expected usage, and acceptable retention terms during a documented discovery conversation.

stages.label: Validated economics
stages.value: 40 organizations pass workload and spread checks
stages.detail: Half of qualified organizations supplies an authorized benchmark or traffic sample. Compare effective unit costs, p95 latency, retry burden, and minimum-commit exposure.

stages.label: Funded pilots
stages.value: 20 organizations prepay bounded production pilot balances
stages.detail: Half of validated organizations accepts the service terms and funds a capped pilot. Record wallet liability separately from recognized revenue and enforce hard usage limits.

stages.label: Repeat consumption
stages.value: 10 organizations complete a second paid cycle
stages.detail: Half of funded pilots consumes delivered service and purchases another cycle. Expand commitments only against observed repeat demand and customer concentration limits.

diagrams.title: Base Case: $675,000 Billings to $189,000 Owner Profit
diagrams.subtitle: Separate upstream pass-through economics from retained operating performance.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Annual USD; canonical retained_share is 0.65. The $168,000 operating-cost and $81,750 variable-cost allocations are illustrative components of the required $249,750 post-upstream cost total. Bars 1, 3, and 6 are absolute totals; bars 2, 4, and 5 are signed movements. Never add the retained subtotal twice.
diagrams.caption: $675,000 − $236,250 = $438,750 retained contribution; $438,750 − $168,000 − $81,750 = $189,000 owner profit. Profit is 28.0% of gross billings and 43.08% of retained contribution. The scorecard's ASC 606 net presentation assumes an agent arrangement; assess principal-versus-agent status separately for each promised service.

stages.label: Gross customer billings
stages.value: $675,000 annual delivered compute and telecom billings
stages.detail: Opening total equals $56,250 monthly on an annualized basis. These are operator customer billings, not customers' underlying commerce, token resale proceeds, or enterprise revenue.

stages.label: Upstream capacity cost
stages.value: Subtract $236,250 for upstream capacity and termination
stages.detail: Thirty-five percent of gross billings goes to supplier capacity and carrier termination, including the modeled effect of commits. Do not deduct these charges again below.

stages.label: Retained contribution
stages.value: $438,750 remains after the upstream supplier deduction
stages.detail: Subtotal equals 65% of gross billings and $36,562.50 monthly. Use this denominator for the retained-margin view; it is not the owner's take-home profit.

stages.label: Recurring operating costs
stages.value: Subtract $168,000 for recurring pod and platform operations
stages.detail: Illustrative expense envelope equals $14,000 monthly, the canonical range ceiling. Allocate it to contractor support, observability, administration, and recurring tooling.

stages.label: Variable operating costs
stages.value: Subtract $81,750 for variable fulfillment and collection costs
stages.detail: Illustrative annual allocation covers processing fees, chargeback losses, service credits, and non-upstream variable support. Keep these outside the recurring monthly envelope and avoid duplicating supplier capacity charges.

stages.label: Annual owner profit
stages.value: $189,000 remains after all modeled operating deductions
stages.detail: Closing total equals $15,750 monthly on an annualized basis. Preserve the canonical owner-profit convention; personal taxes and an additional imputed owner salary are not separately modeled.

diagrams.title: Compare Retained Yield Before Operating Costs
diagrams.subtitle: Five illustrative product spreads reconcile to the 65% retained-share anchor.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values are retained-contribution percentages, not owner profit margins or observed market quotes. Assigning $135,000 annual gross billings to each of five niches creates an illustrative equal-weight Base mix totaling $675,000.
diagrams.caption: Retained contributions total $91,800 + $83,700 + $101,250 + $74,250 + $87,750 = $438,750. The weighted retained yield is 65%; payment-processing and other operating costs remain below this measure. Actual product mixes require fresh supplier quotes.

stages.label: H100 and H200 reservations
stages.value: 68% retained yield on authorized GPU-hour resale
stages.detail: At $135,000 gross billings, upstream cost is $43,200 and retained contribution is $91,800. Prefer prepaid business balances; idle reserved hours still consume cash.

stages.label: B200 capacity windows
stages.value: 62% retained yield on bounded accelerated-compute windows
stages.detail: At $135,000 gross billings, upstream cost is $51,300 and retained contribution is $83,700. Match customer reservation terms to supply; benchmark before promising throughput.

stages.label: Multi-provider inference
stages.value: 75% retained yield on normalized delivered inference
stages.detail: At $135,000 gross billings, upstream cost is $33,750 and retained contribution is $101,250. Meter input, output, cache, and retries separately before debiting prepaid credits.

stages.label: SIP and business messaging
stages.value: 55% retained yield after carrier and messaging charges
stages.detail: At $135,000 gross billings, upstream cost is $60,750 and retained contribution is $74,250. Include carrier surcharges and registration costs consistently; restrict high-cost destinations and abnormal traffic.

stages.label: Authorized IPv4 leasing
stages.value: 65% retained yield on documented address-capacity leases
stages.detail: At $135,000 gross billings, upstream cost is $47,250 and retained contribution is $87,750. Verify lease authority, routing authorization, abuse history, and return conditions before accepting customer funds.

diagrams.title: Four Pre-Flight Checks Before Customer Traffic
diagrams.subtitle: Each service follows every applicable branch; unresolved checks block that service.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values indicate check order, not risk probabilities. Evaluate the operator's actual role, destination, service, and contract terms. Telecom requirements do not automatically apply to a compute-only product.
diagrams.caption: A pass permits movement to the next applicable check. A failed check sends the affected service back for remediation, not around the control. Recheck changed customers, destinations, providers, and product capabilities.

stages.label: Capacity and workload rights
stages.value: Pass only with authorized supply and screened workloads
stages.detail: Verify resale rights and EAR applicability under 15 CFR parts 742 and 744, including relevant end-user and end-use restrictions. Test tenant isolation and upstream retention settings; otherwise withhold the affected workload or zero-retention offering.

stages.label: Voice provider obligations
stages.value: Pass only after role-specific authentication and mitigation checks
stages.detail: Map the service role to 47 CFR 64.6301 and 64.6305 for applicable STIR/SHAKEN, Robocall Mitigation Database certification, and traffic-acceptance duties. Verify supplier status and traceback procedures; unresolved requirements block voice activation.

stages.label: Messaging and calling use
stages.value: Pass only with documented lawful traffic and carrier registration
stages.detail: Apply 47 U.S.C. 227 and 47 CFR 64.1200 to covered traffic, including applicable permission, revocation, and calling restrictions. Complete carrier-required 10DLC TCR brand and campaign registration; registration alone does not establish permission to message.

stages.label: Reporting and exposure
stages.value: Pass only after reporting classification and funding controls
stages.detail: Classify telecom contribution and reporting duties under 47 CFR 54.706 and 54.711 using current FCC Form 499-A instructions; contribution exemptions do not automatically remove filing duties. Confirm prepaid limits, refund rules, chargeback reserves, and emergency traffic shutoff ownership.

diagrams.title: Three Seats Launch; Five Seats Support the Scaled Case
diagrams.subtitle: Keep commercial authority, platform execution, and telecom operations explicit.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each numeric value represents one person, not one full-time equivalent. Conservative and Base use 1 FT + 2 C; Scaled uses 2 FT + 3 C. The last two seats are additions, not initial hires.
diagrams.caption: Conservative: $150,000 gross, $97,500 retained, $27,000 owner profit; margins 18% gross and 27.69% retained. Base: $675,000 gross, $438,750 retained, $189,000 profit; margins 28.0% and 43.08%. Scaled: $1,200,000 gross, $780,000 retained, $456,000 profit; margins 38% and 58.46%. Retained share stays 65%.

stages.label: Owner and commercial lead
stages.value: Initial full-time seat owns commitments and customer economics
stages.detail: Set pricing floors, negotiate supplier rights, maintain cash forecasts, and resolve customer concentration exposure. Authorize commitment increases only after reviewing utilization, churn, and available operating cash.

stages.label: Platform engineering contractor
stages.value: Initial contractor owns routing, isolation, and usage integrity
stages.detail: Maintain LiteLLM or vLLM, tenant controls, DCGM collection, idempotent wallet debits, and usage reconciliation. Publish tested incident runbooks and instrument supplier-cost drift.

stages.label: Telecom operations contractor
stages.value: Initial contractor owns carrier provisioning and traffic exceptions
stages.detail: Maintain SIP least-cost routes, carrier limits, 10DLC provisioning records, traceback responses, and applicable filing calendars. Escalate suspicious traffic immediately rather than waiting for monthly settlement.

stages.label: Customer operations specialist
stages.value: Scaled addition supplies the second full-time operating seat
stages.detail: Own onboarding, support queues, renewal preparation, and service-credit evidence. Add this seat when measured support load threatens response targets and retained contribution can support the recurring expense.

stages.label: Security and reconciliation contractor
stages.value: Scaled addition supplies the third contracted specialist seat
stages.detail: Independently sample access controls, supplier invoices, wallet balances, and abuse investigations. Separate reconciliation review from the person changing rates or issuing customer credits.

diagrams.title: Allocate $10,000–$60,000 Before Expanding Commitments
diagrams.subtitle: Four buckets illustrate a $30,000 working launch budget.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values show the $30,000 reference allocation in USD. Each stage also gives low-capital and upper-capital allocations; the three complete budgets total $10,000, $30,000, and $60,000. These are capital envelopes, not annual expense forecasts.
diagrams.caption: Low budget: $4,000 + $2,500 + $2,000 + $1,500 = $10,000. Reference budget: $12,000 + $8,000 + $6,000 + $4,000 = $30,000. Upper budget: $24,000 + $16,000 + $12,000 + $8,000 = $60,000. Customer prepaid balances remain service obligations, not free capital.

stages.label: Supplier deposits and first capacity
stages.value: $12,000 reference allocation for bounded upstream supply access
stages.detail: Allocate $4,000 at the low budget and $24,000 at the upper budget. Favor cancellable pilot capacity; record refundable deposits separately from consumed services and do not treat the deposit as recurring profit expense.

stages.label: Settlement and loss reserve
stages.value: $8,000 reference allocation for timing gaps and service losses
stages.detail: Allocate $2,500 at the low budget and $16,000 at the upper budget. Cover supplier settlement timing, refunds, and chargeback exposure with operator cash rather than assuming card-funded wallets cannot reverse.

stages.label: Metering and tenant controls
stages.value: $6,000 reference allocation for instrumentation and containment work
stages.detail: Allocate $2,000 at the low budget and $12,000 at the upper budget. Implement wallet reconciliation, scoped credentials, routing limits, workload isolation tests, and retention verification before raising usage ceilings.

stages.label: Onboarding and operating setup
stages.value: $4,000 reference allocation for qualified pilots and service setup
stages.detail: Allocate $1,500 at the low budget and $8,000 at the upper budget. Fund supplier diligence, applicable registrations, contract review, and narrowly targeted pilot acquisition. Release spending against completed operating evidence.

diagrams.title: Build the Evidence for a First Deal in 30 Days
diagrams.subtitle: Four weekly milestones prepare a controlled commercial launch.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values are milestone end days. The canonical time to first deal remains 1–4 months; this sprint establishes readiness and can finish before the first paid customer arrives.
diagrams.caption: Sequence supply validation, metering, buyer qualification, and bounded activation. Do not convert an unfinished test, pending registration, or unsigned supplier offer into a completed launch claim.

stages.label: Days 1-7
stages.value: Select one wedge and verify supplier economics
stages.detail: Choose one GPU, inference, or telecom product. Obtain written resale terms and comparable supplier quotes, classify applicable service duties, and model utilization break-even without treating prepaid deposits as revenue.

stages.label: Days 8-14
stages.value: Build the wallet, meter, and controlled shutdown path
stages.detail: Connect a Stripe test flow to an internal credit ledger. Replay duplicate events, supplier outages, and exhausted balances; test tenant isolation and retention settings before enabling customer production credentials.

stages.label: Days 15-21
stages.value: Qualify buyers and prove a bounded service benchmark
stages.detail: Conduct discovery with named buyers and benchmark authorized workloads or traffic. Complete applicable carrier provisioning and registrations, document service limits, and reject pilots whose effective unit economics fail the price floor.

stages.label: Days 22-30
stages.value: Run an eligible pilot or finish readiness evidence
stages.detail: If contracts, funding, and applicable service requirements are complete, activate a capped pilot and reconcile daily. Otherwise finish test evidence and buyer follow-up without buying speculative capacity or claiming a completed deal.
